steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another — e.g. £1 = $1.25. Determined by supply and demand in the foreign exchange market. | Key Fact: Appreciation: pound becomes stronger (buys more foreign currency). Depreciation: pound becomes weaker (buys less). | Key Fact: Appreciation: imports cheaper (good for consumers), exports more expensive (bad for UK exporters), overseas holidays cheaper. | Key Fact: Depreciation: imports more expensive (inflationary), exports cheaper (boosting export demand), overseas holidays cost more.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how an exchange rate is determined through supply and demand. | Analyse how a depreciation of the pound would affect UK exporters and consumers buying imports. | Evaluate whether a strong pound is good for the UK economy.
